title: Softtech Engineers Ltd - 543470 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Softtech Q4 FY26 revenue rose 50% YoY to INR 46.6 crore and FY26 EBITDA margin reached 24%, with a target of INR 300 crore revenue in three years.
summary.overview: Softtech reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR 46.6 crore (up 50% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 10 crore at a 21% margin, and PAT of INR 2.7 crore against INR 0.1 crore a year earlier. For FY26, revenue grew 40% to INR 132.9 crore, EBITDA rose 45% to INR 32.2 crore (24% margin), and PAT reached INR 5.3 crore. Management said the order book is about INR 232 crore and the pipeline about INR 436 crore, and it set a three-year target of INR 300 crore revenue at 25-30% EBITDA margin. The call covered the new TDR exchange mandate in Mumbai, the Airport Authority of India project, and the Germany and US expansion, with several answers left vague on numbers.

segments.name: CivitPERMIT (flagship permitting)
segments.commentary: About 50% of FY26 revenue; management expects a similar share in FY27, with transaction-based projects going live adding to it.

segments.name: CivitINFRA (infrastructure project monitoring)
segments.commentary: About 25% of FY26 revenue; expected to hold at the same level or dip slightly in FY27.

segments.name: CivitBUILD, BIM and GIS services and others
segments.commentary: Together about 15-20% of revenue, per management's split.

segments.name: CivitTDR (Mumbai TDR exchange)
segments.commentary: Mandatory on the BMC platform from 10 May 2026; Softtech earns 0.5% per transaction. FY26 BMC TDR transaction value was about INR 8,000 crore, and management cited 70-80% margins.

guidance_outlook: Target revenue of about INR 300 crore within three years (FY29), with EBITDA margin of at least 25-30%; management said 'conservatively' 28-30%.
FY27 revenue growth target of 25-27%; management also said it is targeting 20% normal growth in existing businesses, with TDR as upside.
Management said 50% of revenue should come from India over the next three years, with overseas growing faster.
Germany: management expects commercial traction about six months after prototyping, with news possibly in Q3-Q4 of this calendar year.
Airport Authority of India order: about 40% of the roughly INR 17 crore value recognised in FY26; the remaining 60% expected over about three years as AMC.
capex_capacity: Team of about 550 people, of whom about 70% are in R&D, implementation and related roles; business development has 25-30 people.
Intangibles (about INR 70 crore), intangibles under development (about INR 19 crore) are capitalised product development, amortised over three to four years.
Subsidiary set up in Germany via acquisition of a company held by Sandy Moser; a German sales leader has been hired and more recruitment is under way.
Management said headcount growth will be well below revenue growth, with some specialist hires for metaverse and AI.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR 232 crore; management said about 60% will convert to revenue this year, of which about 40% is recurring.
Opportunity pipeline about INR 436 crore; management puts conversion probability above 60%, and Softtech has won about 70% of bids it chooses to pursue.

TDR: 100-odd registrations so far and some transactions; the platform became mandatory for Mumbai TDR transactions from 10 May 2026, and management expects volumes to pick up over the next 2-4 months.
Airport Authority of India: first phase completed and appreciated by the Civil Aviation Minister; a one-time licence model, with further phases possible.
CivitSUSTAIN: first order from Mitsubishi for a Delhi Jal Board water-network project; GIFT City is still awaiting a mandate.
Oman tender: Softtech is L2 on price and T1 on technology, but lost ground to a Singapore bidder on cost; negotiated bids are with the tender committee.
US: small orders are being won, POCs are done, and a partner has been signed. Revenue was small in FY26 and is expected to rise in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is the order book split between transaction and project revenue, and what is the pipeline conversion rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 60% of the roughly INR 200 crore order book will be booked this year, of which about 40% is recurring. It put pipeline conversion above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the provisions rise from INR 45 lakh to about INR 2.5 crore, and is this recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Bang said a new policy was started last year to provide for government retentions and deposits (about 1-2% of invoices). He also said gratuity liability rose after the revised Labour Code took effect in November 2025. Management said some amounts will be recovered and reversed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TDR revenue model and the size of the opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Softtech earns 0.5% of each transaction on the TDR exchange. FY26 BMC transactions were about INR 8,000 crore, implying about INR 40 crore in gross fees at that volume. Margins were put at 70-80% after data-centre and maintenance costs. MMRDA, MSRDC, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar and Thane are excluded.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR 17 crore Airport Authority order is recognised in FY26, and is it a SaaS model?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40% was recognised in FY26; the rest is expected over about three years as AMC. Management called it a one-time licence, with further phases possible.

qa_highlights.question: How does Softtech plan to grow in Germany and what is the RIB/Thomas Wolf relationship?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier RIB link was purely financial via convertible debentures. Thomas Wolf now invests through his family fund and the German subsidiary is 100% owned. Management expects German commercial traction in about six months, with news in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix and growth outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CivitPERMIT is expected at about 50%, CivitINFRA at about 25% (flat or slightly lower), and the rest from CivitBUILD, BIM and GIS services at 15-20%. FY27 growth target is 25-27%, with a higher EBITDA margin only as far as TDR lifts it.

qa_highlights.question: How defensible is the product as AI lowers replication barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 15 years of government permit datasets, the 12-agent CivitTwin AI platform, and deep enterprise penetration as barriers. It said headcount need not rise in step with revenue.

risks_watch: Government receivables are slow: management said government collections take time and some retentions may take up to seven years. Watch DSO (260 days) and provisioning.
Oman tender outcome is uncertain, with the Singapore bidder lower on cost and the war adding uncertainty.
TDR revenue depends on BMC mandate adoption; management did not give a firm FY27 TDR revenue figure. Watch transaction volumes over the next 2-4 months.
Management declined to disclose customer churn and gave only a rough 70/30 win/loss guide, so the churn data is weak.
Germany and US revenue are still unquantified; management said US revenue was little in FY26.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the growth story (TDR, AI platform, INR 300 crore target), but vague or deferring on hard numbers: TDR FY27 revenue, Germany revenue, churn, and the cause of the provisions were not quantified. Deepak Bang gave the most concrete figures.
key_quotes: Over the next three to four years, I am targeting that we touch a number of about INR 300 crores, as a revenue without really losing the focus onto the profitability
So the probability level of conversions here are very high, more than about 60% is what I can close it with the numbers.
we are targeting a normal growth of 20% into all ongoing businesses.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-27% (midpoint 26%) and INR 300 cr revenue targeted by FY29, backed by an INR 232 cr order book (about 60% converting this year) and a INR 436 cr pipeline, but no specific capacity additions and several answers were vague on numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY26 EBITDA margin was 24% (Q4 21%) and management targets 25-30% over three years, with TDR at 70-80% margins as the lift, but it gave no firm FY27 margin figure and provisions rose from INR 45 lakh to about INR 2.5 crore, a drag that may recur.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches discussed; management said headcount growth will be well below revenue growth on a ~550-person team, so growth comes from existing capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-27%, with about 60% of the INR 232 crore order book converting this year and TDR volumes expected to pick up over 2-4 months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; capitalised product development (INR 70 crore intangibles, INR 19 crore under development) is ongoing, but no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called the 28-30% margin 'conservative' and sees TDR as upside to the 20% base growth, but it gave no firm FY27 TDR revenue figure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Government receivables are slow (DSO 260 days, retentions up to seven years), the Oman tender is at risk to a Singapore bidder on cost, and the US and Germany revenue is unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TDR goes live on the BMC mandate from 10 May 2026, the CivitSUSTAIN Delhi Jal Board water-network order is starting, and metaverse and AI specialist hires point to new offerings, though no launch dates were given.

rows.label: Germany commercial traction via acquired subsidiary
rows.why: Management expects commercial traction about six months after prototyping, with news possibly in Q3-Q4 of this calendar year; no revenue quantified.

rows.label: Order book conversion of INR 232 crore
rows.why: About 60% of the INR 232 crore order book (about INR 140 crore) is expected to convert to revenue this year, of which 40% is recurring, and pipeline conversion is above 60%.

rows.label: TDR transaction volume ramp on BMC mandate
rows.why: Mandatory on BMC platform from 10 May 2026 with FY26 transaction value about INR 8,000 crore and 0.5% fee (about INR 40 crore gross), but no FY27 TDR revenue figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the TDR mandate, the INR 300 crore target and the 25-27% FY27 growth guide, but deferred on hard numbers (TDR revenue, Germany and US revenue, churn, the cause of provisions); analysts pressed on provisions and the order book split.
